Wait/record lifetime comparison: exact Wait creates a branch-local CordDataSocketClass record in its data loop and a branch-local CordListenSocketClass record in its separate listening loop, with ArrayList::get filling each by value before getFD and storing its Socket. Pump likewise fills a branch-local value record before selecting Socket and the per-record fields, but branches within a single combined loop and handles get failure. In baseline and retail Pump both copy all four data-record dwords and all three listening-record dwords; record scratch locations overlap across the mutually exclusive paths. Retail's data record stores at esp+0x70 and +0x78 where baseline stores at esp+0x68 and +0x70, consistent with the broader shifted frame, not proof of extra record fields or simultaneous live records. Moving both records outward to force independent live slots would contradict the observed shared slots and needlessly extend lifetimes. Wait has no profiling object, receive loop, log buffers or inlined Send_Go_Away; its exactness therefore establishes the record copy idiom but does not identify Pump's missing two dwords. Existing history already tried moving loop locals/texts/len/type/i/from with no change. Xtime construction cannot be hoisted to increase lifetime because that changes when the clock is read; forcing additional objects or reads would be artificial. The actual go-away argument lifetime and unsigned type changes tested here optimize identically, while direct handler tests worsen the frame-independent comparison. I found no further distinct, supported local lifetime mechanism for the missing slots in this pass; a new observation identifying a real live local or reusable helper is required, and group review may supply one.
